newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Global rubber pact in limbo without Italy support.
newsitem.headline: Global rubber pact in limbo without Italy support.

text.p: A new world rubber price pact is short of endorsement from just one country, Italy, after Malaysia and Indonesia set aside a dispute to ratify the pact, officials said on Tuesday.

"Italy said they would ratify the agreement by the end of the deadline on 31 December last year but we haven't got word of them doing it," James Hegarty, buffer stock manager for the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO), told Reuters.
INRO will be the administrator for the International Natural Rubber Agreement 3 (INRA 3), which was scheduled to come into force on January 1.

INRA 3, a United Nations-brokered pact, is the world's only remaining global commodity agreement with economic provisions and a buffer stock that allows the industry to buy and sell rubber to stabilise prices.

The agreement was held up previously by Indonesia and Malaysia -- two of the world's largest rubber producers, who both wanted the top executive director's post in INRO in exchange for ratifying the pact.
Hegarty said INRO was notified on Monday by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) that the two countries had fulfilled their obligations to the pact.

He declined to say which country won the tussle for the executive director's post in INRO -- now held by Thailand's Pong Sono. But INRO sources said Malaysia's Primary Industries deputy secretary-general Ahmad Zubeir Noordin had been picked as successor.
Hegarty said Italy's two percent voting rights among INRO's 26 consumer members was vital to make up the minimum 75 percent votes needed to bring the INRA 3 into force.
"The EU (European Union) has already ratified the pact as a joint member and the delay by Italy is surprising," he said.
Hegarty hoped that news of the Italian ratification could be reported by UNCTAD as early as next week.
Hegarty said there was also no news of ratification from China, another consumer, but added that "they don't really make a difference to the pact".
He said INRO's next meeting would be on February 24 to announce the new executive director and oversee other administrative procedures.
